summary: In the interim, the Division has received an application for a new liquor control license from a third party for the premises previously licensed by the Licensee at 823 Wheeler St. Suite 5, Ames, Iowa.  On August 10, 2021, the City of Ames (local authority) denied the liquor license renewal application for Espuelas Inc. d/b/a La Fiesta Bar & Grill (licensee).  DIA No. 22ABD0003 ABD Docket No: D-2021-00077 Page 2 ISSUE Whether the local authority’s decision to deny Espuelas Inc. d/b/a La Fiesta Bar & Grill’s renewal application for a liquor license for 2021-2022 was proper due to evidence that Licensee repeatedly served alcoholic beverages to persons under legal age.  On August 10, 2021, Ames Police Department Lieutenant Heath Ropp sent a letter to Ames Mayor John Haila and Ames City Council Members, recommending that the liquor license renewal for La Fiesta Bar & Grill not be renewed for the next year.  In determining the license applicant’s good moral character, the local authority may review not only convictions, but other factors it deems appropriate.11 The following reason was given for denying Licensee’s liquor license application: The Licensee twice served alcoholic beverages to persons under legal age.

Kim Reynolds Governor of Iowa
Adam Gregg Lieutenant Governor

IN RE:
Espuelas Inc. DOCKET NO. D-2021-00077
d/b/a La Fiesta Bar & Grill
823 Wheeler St. Suite 5 DIA NO. 21ABD0003
Ames, IA 50010
DISMISSAL ORDER
License No. LC0045757
NOW, on this 28th day of September 2022, this matter comes before the Administrator of
the Alcoholic Beverages Division (Division) on his own motion for a determination of the
threshold question of whether the cancellation of Espeulas Inc.’s (Licensee) liquor license moots
its appeal of the City of Ames’ (Local Authority) denial of the renewal of said license. See Riley
Drive Entertainment I, Inc. v. Reynolds, 970 N.W.2d 289, 296 (Iowa 2022) (declaring that
mootness is “a threshold question”); Homan v. Branstad, 864 N.W.2d 321, 327-28 (Iowa 2015)
(“It is our duty on our own motion to refrain from determining moot questions.”).
On August 10, 2021, the City of Ames denied the renewal of the Licensee’s liquor control
license. A timely appeal of the denial was filed by the Licensee and a hearing was held on October
13, 2021, before Administrative Law Judge Tricia A. Johnston. ALJ Johnston issued a Proposed
Decision on November 10, 2021, affirming the Local Authority’s denial of the renewal of the
Licensee’s liquor control license. On December 10, 2021, a timely Notice of Appeal was filed by
the Licensee with the Division Administrator.
The Administrator has recently learned that during the pendency of this appeal, the
Licensee lost control of the premises for which the liquor control license was issued. The
1

Licensee’s license was subsequently cancelled on August 12, 2022. In the interim, the Division
has received an application for a new liquor control license from a third party for the premises
previously licensed by the Licensee at 823 Wheeler St. Suite 5, Ames, Iowa. Through its license
application, the third party has provided proof to the Division that it now exercises exclusive
control over that premises.
For those reasons, the Administrator solicited the parties’ positions as to whether the
Licensee’s appeal should be dismissed as moot. Both parties submitted a response to the
Administrator on September 19, 2022 stating that they had no objection to this case being
dismissed as moot.
ORDER
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED that the Licensee’s appeal of the Local Authorities’
denial of the renewal of its liquor control license is hereby DISMISSED as moot.
The parties are hereby notified that pursuant to Iowa Code § 17A.19, this Order constitutes
final agency action for the purpose of Iowa Code chapters 17A and 123. This Order becomes final,
unless a party to the hearing files a Petition for Judicial Review with the Iowa District Court within
30 days from the date of this Order.

STATE OF IOWA
BEFORE THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE
ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES DIVISION
In the Matter of: DOCKET NO. D-2021-00077
DIA NO. 22ABD0003
Espuelas Inc.
d/b/a La Fiesta Bar & Grill
823 Wheeler St. Suite 5
Ames, IA 50010, PROPOSED DECISION
Liquor License No. LC0045757
On August 10, 2021, the City of Ames (local authority) denied the liquor license
renewal application for Espuelas Inc. d/b/a La Fiesta Bar & Grill (licensee). The
reasons for the denial were listed on the form. (Exhibit A). The licensee filed a
timely appeal, and a hearing was held before Administrative Law Judge Tricia A.
Johnston on October 13, 2021 at 9:00 a.m. Ames City Attorney Jane Chang
represented the local authority. Ames City Clerk Diane Voss and Ames Police
Department Commander Jason Tuttle were called as witnesses and presented
testimony. The sole owner of Licensee, Luis Salazar, appeared with counsel,
Andrew Meyer, and presented testimony. At Appellant’s request, a Spanish
language interpreter was present as standby. Mr. Salazar did not utilize the
interpreter’s assistance at hearing.
THE RECORD
The record includes the Division’s Electronic License Renewal Application; the
Division’s August 27, 2021 Right To Appeal; Notice of Appeal; Acknowledgement
of Appeal; Notice of Hearing; testimony of City Clerk Diane Voss; testimony of
Commander Jason Tuttle, testimony of Luis Salazar, and the following exhibits:
Exhibit A: Letter dated 8/10/21 from Lieutenant Heath Ropp to Mayor
Haila and Ames City Council members regarding the liquor license
renewal for La Fiesta.
Exhibit B: Copy of citation and adjudication record from State v. Alberto
Amezcu Carillo, Story County Case No. STA0143906
Exhibit C: Copy of citation and adjudication record from State v. Alberto
Amezcu Carillo, Story County Case No. STA0144911
Exhibit D: Copy of ABD order dated 5/26/21, in Docket Number D-2021-
00077

DIA No. 22ABD0003
ABD Docket No: D-2021-00077
Page 2
ISSUE
Whether the local authority’s decision to deny Espuelas Inc. d/b/a La Fiesta Bar
& Grill’s renewal application for a liquor license for 2021-2022 was proper due to
evidence that Licensee repeatedly served alcoholic beverages to persons under
legal age.
FINDINGS OF FACT
Espuelas Inc., d/b/a La Fiesta Bar & Grill, holds a Class C Liquor License LC-
0045757 for the premises located in Ames, Iowa. Luis Salazar is the 100% owner.
The record does not reflect that Salazar has had any criminal convictions related
to his ownership of La Fiesta Bar & Grill. There was no evidence presented to
suggest the licensee is not now current in the payment of all taxes and utilities.
The evidence does not reflect that the liquor license has been suspended or
otherwise sanctioned for any liquor law violations. (Exh. A; Exh. B; Tuttle
testimony; Voss testimony; Salazar testimony).
The Licensee applied for renewal of its liquor license for a one-year license to
commence on August 19, 2021 and end on August 18, 2022. On August 10, 2021,
Ames Police Department Lieutenant Heath Ropp sent a letter to Ames Mayor
John Haila and Ames City Council Members, recommending that the liquor
license renewal for La Fiesta Bar & Grill not be renewed for the next year. The
letter informed the Mayor and City Council verbatim as follows:
A review of police records for the past 12 months found two liquor law
violations for the above business. During a compliance check on April 22,
2021 an employee sold alcohol to a minor and was cited accordingly. A
follow-up compliance check was completed on June 9th, 2021 and the
same employee sold alcohol to a minor again and was cited accordingly for
the second time.
So far, the Police Department has made recommendations to improve
their performance such as asking for customer identification and verifying
customer age, as well as utilizing the Iowa ABD Age to Purchase mobile
application to scan identifications to ensure validity.
At this time, the Police Department would not recommend a
renewal of La Fiesta Bar & Grill’s license for the next year.
However, the Police Department would be in favor of the
issuance of a 6-month license to give the business and the Police
Department a shorter period of time to evaluate changes to
ensure due diligence in keeping underage patrons from
obtaining alcohol. The process to initiate this would be for the City

DIA No. 22ABD0003
ABD Docket No: D-2021-00077
Page 3
Council to deny the requested 12-month license and adopt a motion
indicating the City Council would accept a six-month license application.
During this 6-month period, the Police Department will continue to
monitor the above location by conducting regular foot patrols, bar checks
and by educating the bar staff through trainings and quarterly meetings.
(Ex. A) (emphasis as in original).
The Licensee’s application was added to the City Council agenda for the meeting
which took place on August 24, 2021. Ames Police Commander Jason Tuttle was
present for that meeting as was the Licensee’s then manager, Amezcu Alberto
Carillo. The Council unanimously voted to deny the one-year license renewal for
the Licensee. Diane Voss testified on behalf of the local authority that the City
Council had previously denied a one-year license renewal for Patty’s Irish Pub on
March 9, 2021 for the same reason. That establishment came back and applied
for a six-month license which it received. Voss further testified that another
establishment’s one-year license renewal application was also denied on August
24, 2021 for the same reason. (Voss testimony; Tuttle testimony).
The Local Authority wrote “due to violations” as the basis for Licensee’s renewal
application denial. In its notes regarding the denial, it was noted that the “City
Council approved a 6 month license going forward. Applicant will need to apply
for new 6 month license.” (sic). (Application).
Appellant was notified by letter, dated August 27, 2021, of the denial of the
renewal application, however the six-month license eligibility was not noted in
that letter. The letter informed Licensee of its appeal rights. Licensee timely
appealed the Local Authority’s denial on August 30, 2021. As of the date of
hearing, Voss testified that the Licensee had not applied for a six-month license
renewal. (Right to Appeal letter; Request for Appeal; Voss testimony).
The Local Authority provided copies of the two citations and convictions at issue
regarding Amezcu Alberto Carrillo serving alcohol to a minor on April 22, 2021
and June 9, 2021. (Ex. B; Ex. C). On May 26, 2021, the Alcoholic Beverages
Division Ordered Licensee to pay a civil penalty of $500 as a penalty for violation
of Iowa Code section 123.49(2)(h) for sale of alcohol to minors. (Ex. D).
Commander Tuttle testified regarding his recommendation and the council’s
denial of the Licensee’s renewal application. Tuttle stated when he spoke at the
city council meeting, he recommended to the council that the one-year license be
denied and the business be directed to apply for a six-month license, due to
having two violations for selling alcohol to a minor. Tuttle noted the same
employee, Amezcu Carrillo, made both sales. Tuttle stated he made this
recommendation in order to provide a shorter period during which they could
evaluate any progress the Licensee would make and would work with the
Licensee to make improvements. (Tuttle testimony).

DIA No. 22ABD0003
ABD Docket No: D-2021-00077
Page 4
Tuttle explained that these citations arose out of compliance checks as part of the
program with the Alcoholic Beverages Division. If a licensee sells to a minor,
they have to do a second check to see if the licensee has come into compliance.
They started compliance checks on March 25, 2021 with all businesses. They did
the first check on Licensee on April 22, 2021. The second compliance check was
done on June 9, 2021 for Licensee. The last compliance check they did as part of
this program was on June 11, 2021. (Tuttle testimony).
Tuttle stated Carrillo attended the meeting and spoke with him afterward. Tuttle
explained to Carrillo how to apply again through the ABD and to have the owner
call him. Carrillo was at the time, the manager of Licensee. Tuttle was unaware
of any other violations by Licensee. (Tuttle testimony).
Tuttle explained at hearing that every time there is a violation, they review each
business. He knew of six businesses who failed checks both times and felt the
council needed to be consistent with these cases. There were two businesses on
August 24, 2021 that they voted on, and the other four would be voted on in the
future. Tuttle stated he made the same recommendation for each one; denial of
the one-year license renewal and advising the licensee to apply for a six-month
license. (Tuttle testimony).
Licensee, Luis Salazar, testified at hearing, stating he had applied for a six-month
license. He explained that Carrillo, the employee that sold to minors, had since
been fired. Salazar stated he had no other violations in the past two years. He
stated he has been working with the licensing division to keep complying. He
fired the manager, Carrillo, to make sure it wouldn’t happen again and has been
training employees regarding compliance. Salazar stated they have always done
training but now they do it more often and remind employees more often. He
further stated he shows employees videos and tells them they need to pay
attention, know the law, and check ID’s. Salazar stated they train on fake ID’s
and tell employees to make sure to ask for an ID and to look at the dates. He
stated that he tells employees to make sure they pay attention every time they
serve. He did a training the last week of January with another person from a
restaurant in Nebraska and attends meetings to do things better. (Salazar
testimony).
CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
The Iowa Alcoholic Beverages Control Act (Iowa Code chapter 123) protects the
welfare, health, peace, morals and safety of the people of the state, and all its
provisions shall be liberally construed for the accomplishment of this purpose.1
The local authority asserts that the licensee’s license should not be renewed based
upon two violations of Iowa Code 123.49(2)(h) (2021), providing alcohol to a
1 Iowa Code section 123.1 (2019).

DIA No. 22ABD0003
ABD Docket No: D-2021-00077
Page 5
minor. The issue before the undersigned is not a revocation or suspension of the
license. The Local Authority denied the renewal of a license and therefore the
burden is on the licensee to establish compliance with the requirements for
holding a liquor license in the state of Iowa.2
As part of the application process, the applicant must provide a statement asserting
whether any of the business’ officers, directors, or persons owning or controlling ten
percent or more of the stock, or having a financial interest in the business, have ever
been convicted of any offense against the laws of the U.S. or any state or territory
thereof, or any political subdivision.3 At hearing, it was not disputed that Mr.
Salazar is the sole owner of the establishment and, as of this date, has not been
convicted of any offense.
As a general matter, a liquor control license may only be issued to a person who is
of “good moral character” as defined by Iowa Code chapter 123. 4 "Person of good
moral character" is defined, in part, to mean that the person has such financial
standing and “good reputation” as will satisfy the administrator that the person
will comply with this chapter and all laws, ordinances, and regulations applicable
to the person's operations under this chapter.5 A liquor license “shall not be issued
for premises which do not conform to all applicable laws, ordinances, resolutions,
and health and fire regulations.”6
A person holding a liquor control license and the person’s agents or employees
shall not sell give or otherwise supply any alcoholic beverage to any person
knowing or failing to exercise reasonable care to ascertain whether the person is
under legal age.7 Any person who violates this provision commits a simple
misdemeanor. If any liquor control licensee is convicted of a violation of this
section, the administrator or local authority shall, in addition to criminal
penalties fixed for violations by this section, assess a civil penalty. A first
violation shall result in a civil penalty in the amount of $500.00. A second
violation within two years shall result in a 30-day suspension and a civil penalty
in the amount of $1,500.00. A third violation within three years shall result in a
sixty-day suspension and a fourth violation shall result in revocation of the
permit. 8
As pertinent to this case, all applicants for liquor control licenses shall comply
with the following requirements, where applicable, prior to receiving a liquor
2 Iowa Code section 123.32(6)(2021). See also Tony’s Tap, Inc. v. Dep’t of Commerce,
2005 WL 1397515 at *2 (Iowa Ct. App. 2005).
3 Iowa Code section 123.31 (2021).
4 Iowa Code section 123.30(1)(a)(2021).
5 Iowa Code section 123.3(40)(2021) (emphasis added).
6 Iowa Code section 123.30(2)(2021).
7 Iowa Code section 123.49(2)(h) (2021).
8 Iowa Code section 123.50(2) & (3)(2021).

DIA No. 22ABD0003
ABD Docket No: D-2021-00077
Page 6
license, wine permit, or beer permit: cleanliness of premises; toilet facilities,
water, financial standing and reputation. The Iowa Administrative Code provides
that “[a] local authority or the administrator may consider an applicant’s
financial standing and good reputation in addition to the other requirements and
conditions for obtaining a liquor control license… and the local authority or the
administrator shall disapprove or deny an application for a liquor control
license… if the applicant fails to demonstrate that the applicant complies with
the lawful requirements and conditions for holding the license, permit or
certificate of compliance.”9
When evaluating an applicant’s “good reputation,” the local authority or
administrator “may consider such factors as, but not limited to, the following…
pattern or practice of sales of alcoholic beverages to 19- and 20-year old persons
for which the licensee or permittee, the licensee’s or permittee’s agents or
employees, have pled or have been found guilty, pattern and practice by the
licensee or permittee, or the licensee’s or permittee’s agents or employees, of
violating alcoholic beverages laws and regulations for which corrective action has
been taken since the previous license or permit was issued, licensee or permittee
misdemeanor convictions, the recency of the misdemeanor convictions.”10 In
determining the license applicant’s good moral character, the local authority may
review not only convictions, but other factors it deems appropriate.11
The following reason was given for denying Licensee’s liquor license application:
The Licensee twice served alcoholic beverages to persons under legal age. It is a
violation of Iowa Code section 123.49 for a licensee or a licensee’s agents or
employee to sell, give or otherwise supply any alcoholic beverage to any person,
knowing or failing to exercise reasonable care to ascertain whether the person is
under legal age.12 This does qualify as a violation of the alcoholic beverages laws
and regulations and calls into question Licensee’s good reputation in that the
licensee has not demonstrated that he will comply with this chapter and all laws,
ordinances, and regulations applicable to Licensee’s operations under this
chapter.13
The undersigned notes that the manager in question is no longer an employee of the
Licensee, having been fired for his repeated violation of this provision.
Furthermore, Mr. Salazar explained the measures he has taken to train his
employees and insure that this does not happen again. It was noted at hearing that
no further violations have occurred.
9 185 Iowa Administrative Code (IAC) 4.2(1)-(4). (emphasis added).
10 185 Iowa Administrative Code (IAC) 4.2(4)”b.” (emphasis added).
11 PR Pub, LLC d/b/a the Quarry v. Iowa Alcoholic Beverages Division 2014 WL 1494959
*5 (Iowa Ct. App. April 16, 2014)
12 Iowa Code section 123.49(2) (h) (2021).
13 Iowa Code section 123.3(40)(2021).

DIA No. 22ABD0003
ABD Docket No: D-2021-00077
Page 7
Licensee argues that allowing him to apply for a six-month license rather than a
one-year license is arbitrary. The Local Authority’s stated position that they would
approve a six-month license is not before the undersigned as it has not occurred.
What has occurred, and what has been appealed, is the local authority’s decision to
deny a one-year license.
As noted, the burden to show eligibility to hold a liquor license rests with the
licensee. Licensee’s employee committed two liquor law violations by serving
underage patrons, and Licensee’s employee pled guilty to those offenses. The
statutes and administrative regulations allow the undersigned to consider these
actions, if such actions demonstrate that the Licensee does not have the good
moral character required to hold a liquor license in the State of Iowa.
In evaluating the licensee’s good reputation, it is reasonable to consider the
pattern and practice of the liquor law violations by the licensee’s manager which
established that the licensee does not have such good reputation as will satisfy
the administrator that it will comply with all laws, statutes, and regulations
governing its operations. Based upon the clear violations of Iowa Code section
123.49(2)(h), the local authority did not abuse its discretion under the statute
and rules and was justified in concluding that the licensee has not demonstrated
that he will comply with this chapter and all laws, ordinances, and regulations
applicable to Licensee’s operations under this chapter.
DECISION AND ORDER
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED that the decision of the City of Ames to deny the
renewal application for Liquor License LC0045757 filed by Espuelas Incl, d/b/a
La Fiesta Bar & Grill, is hereby AFFIRMED.
The Iowa Administrative Code at 185 IAC 10.27(1) and (2) provides that any
adversely affected party may appeal a proposed decision to the Administrator of
the Alcoholic Beverages Division within thirty (30) days after issuance of the
proposed decision. In addition, the Administrator may initiate review of a
proposed decision on the Administrator's own motion at any time within thirty
(30) days following the issuance of a proposed decision.
Requests for review shall be sent to the Administrator of the Alcoholic Beverages
Division, 1918 S.E. Hulsizer, Ankeny, IA 50021. Unless otherwise ordered, each
appealing party may file exceptions and briefs within thirty (30) days of the
notice of appeal or order for review. Within thirty (30) days thereafter, any party
may file a responsive brief. The Administrator may shorten or extend the
briefing period as appropriate. The Administrator may resolve the appeal on the
briefs or provide an opportunity for oral argument. 185 IAC 10.27(6). The
administrator may affirm, reverse or modify the proposed decision.

DIA No. 22ABD0003
ABD Docket No: D-2021-00077
Page 8
A party who is adversely affected by the proposed decision shall not be deemed to
have exhausted administrative remedies unless the adversely affected party files a
request for review of the proposed decision within the time provided and the
Administrator has reviewed the proposed decision and has affirmed, reversed, or
modified the proposed decision.
